Seventeen comments

I first heard this on a Michael Coleman recording but was inspired to learn it after hearing Seamus Ennis play it on the whistle, it goes pretty high on fiddle I just slide up into second postion for those high C’s in the high bar. It works great on the whistle I cran the low D on the part that dips below D. It’s a little challenging at first, but hey I think every tune is tough the first couple times through.
This tune has some strange “Reavy-ness” to it, but it’s an old hornpipe that was probably written before Reavy was born.

Have Fun

The Cuckoo, X:8

This is a version I learned at Feakle Festival from Catherine McEvoy. It is more flute-friendly, avoiding the low dips below D. It is most similar to X:4, but differs in various places. I really like how she does the 2nd last bar of the B, where the triplets keep coming back to the A note. She follows it with the Smell of the Bog.

↳ Posted by BansheeWailsOverTheMangoPit on March 3rd, 2020.

Re: The Cuckoo

This is originally an Irish tune, but famous in Cape Breton under the name of Hennessy’s Hornpipe. First played in CB by Angus Chisholm in the Early Recordings album, with the Moonlight Clog, it has been played by great fiddlers such as Ashley MacIsaac, Dan R. MacDonald, and Glenn Graham.

↳ Posted by DòchasLeoA on January 8th, 2024.
